title: Finite orthonormal Fourier basis
statement: Let $\Omega$ and $\iota$ be nonempty finite types, and let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$. A finite Fourier basis consists of a real vector-space basis $\{b_a:a\in\iota\}$ of the functions on $\Omega$, together with a distinguished index $a_0\in\iota$, such that $b_{a_0}$ is the constant-one function and $\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\pi}[b_a(x)b_b(x)]$ equals $1$ when $a=b$ and $0$ otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
The basis indices admit decidable equality
